title: AI-assisted support pilot
purpose: Align on whether to fund a pilot

slides.key_message: Leadership is being asked to decide whether to fund an AI-assisted support pilot.
slides.notes: Decision requested: approve a 250k EUR, six-month AI-assisted support pilot.

slides.key_message: Support costs rose as customer satisfaction and response speed fell.

text.0: Support costs rise as service declines
text.14: Year over year | CSAT scale as provided
text.12:
SUPPORT COSTS
Up 22% year over year
text.15:
CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE
CSAT fell from 84 to 79
Average first response: 14 hours

slides.notes: The combined trend creates a reason to test a focused intervention: support costs are rising while satisfaction and response speed are worsening.

slides.key_message: Repeat questions and document search consume avoidable support capacity.

text.0: Three signals reveal avoidable support work
text.14: Evidence points to repeat questions and answer-finding friction
text.13:
41%
Tickets are repeat questions already answered in the help center
text.18:
35%
Agent time goes to searching internal documents
text.19:
6x
Faster answers on chat; only 18% of tickets arrive there

slides.notes: The chat comparison is relative speed, not a response-time baseline. The 41% figure is the share of all tickets that are repeat help-center questions.

slides.key_message: The proposed pilot tests a lower-cost path than adding agents.

text.0: The AI pilot tests a focused middle path
text.14: Compare the three options on cost and stated service impact
text.13:
DO NOTHING
No added cost
Costs keep rising
text.18:
HIRE 12 AGENTS
About 900k EUR per year
Response time improves to about 8h
text.19:
AI-ASSISTED PILOT
250k EUR for 6 months
Targets: under 4h response; 30% of repeat tickets deflected

slides.notes: The costs and impacts are estimates or targets from the source material, not guaranteed outcomes. No ROI or payback calculation was provided.

slides.key_message: Customers want a straight answer without repeating themselves.

text.14: Survey quote | Pilot hypothesis to test
text.12:
CUSTOMER VOICE
“I just want a straight answer without having to repeat myself three times.”
text.15:
PILOT HYPOTHESIS
AI assistance could make repeat answers easier to find and provide. Test this with customers and agents.

slides.notes: The quotation is reproduced exactly from the supplied survey excerpt. The adjacent statement is a hypothesis for the pilot, not a measured outcome.

slides.key_message: A six-month pilot moves from scope through integration to a rollout decision.

text.15:
Month 1 — Select vendor and scope
Months 2–3 — Integrate with help center and ticketing
Months 4–5 — Run with two support teams
Month 6 — Review results and decide on rollout

slides.notes: The month-by-month sequence and pilot team count are from the proposed plan.

slides.key_message: Quality, adoption, and privacy need explicit checks during the pilot.

text.0: Three risks need gates before launch
text.14: Proposed checks; confirm owners and criteria before kickoff
text.13:
ANSWER QUALITY
Review edge cases; agree when an agent should take over
text.18:
AGENT ADOPTION
Prepare participating teams and gather feedback during the pilot
text.19:
DATA PRIVACY
Complete privacy review before pilot data is used

slides.notes: The three risks come from the source. The checks are proposed mitigations for leadership and the pilot owner to confirm; no owners, thresholds, or review process were supplied.

slides.key_message: The pilot tests faster responses and deflection of repeat questions.

text.0: Pilot success: faster replies, fewer repeats
text.14: Source targets | Baselines shown where provided
text.12:
RESPONSE TIME
Current average: 14 hours
Pilot target: under 4 hours
text.15:
REPEAT QUESTIONS
41% currently repeat help-center questions
Pilot target: deflect 30% of repeat tickets

slides.notes: The source does not specify a measurement method, target for answer quality or agent adoption, or a formal decision threshold. Define these before the pilot begins.
Decision requested: approve 250k EUR for a six-month AI-assisted support pilot. The proposed targets are response time under 4 hours and deflection of 30% of repeat tickets.

slides.key_message: Leadership approval enables the team to begin scoping the pilot.

text.20: Decision requested: approve the 250k EUR pilot

slides.notes: If approved, the proposed first step is to select a vendor and scope during Month 1.
